description: Wasilla's archery scene includes Screaming Eagle Archery Of Alaska, a commercial range that pairs range time with a pro shop and lessons for archers who want to get outfitted and coached under one roof. Alaska's short shooting season and long winters make an indoor or semi-indoor commercial setup like this one valuable for locals who want consistent practice regardless of weather. Whether you're tuning a hunting bow ahead of moose or caribou season or picking up the sport for the first time, the combination of retail support and instruction on-site removes a lot of the guesswork. Contact the range directly for current hours, lesson scheduling, and equipment pricing.

SDT Armory is a commercial archery range in Milford, Connecticut, serving the shoreline area between New Haven and Bridgeport. No pro shop, lesson program, 3D course, or field course is confirmed for this location, so the offering appears to be straightforward lane or range access rather than a full-service archery center. That still makes it a practical option for archers who already own gear and just need a place to shoot regularly in a coastal Connecticut town where dedicated archery space is limited. Reach out to SDT Armory directly to confirm lane availability, hours, and whether walk-ins are welcome before making the trip.

SeiChu Kyudo Kai in Bellevue, Washington carries a name that nods to the Japanese art of kyudo, and it operates as a USA Archery affiliated club running an Adult Archery Program with lessons available. That combination makes it a natural landing spot for grown-up beginners in the Seattle-area suburbs who want structured instruction rather than just open range time. Being USA Archery affiliated also means the club follows a recognized set of safety and coaching standards rather than operating informally. Anyone curious whether the club leans traditional Japanese-style shooting or Olympic recurve fundamentals, or both, should contact SeiChu Kyudo Kai directly to ask about class format and enrollment.

Belton, Texas sits in the fast-growing Bell County corridor between Austin and Waco, and Sendero Shooting Sports is the commercial archery range serving that area. No pro shop, lessons, 3D course, or field course is documented for the location, suggesting it functions primarily as a place to rent or bring your own equipment and shoot lanes. For Central Texas archers who don't need instruction and just want reliable range access, that can be exactly the point. Details on hours, lane pricing, and whether recurve or compound setups are accommodated aren't listed here, so contact Sendero Shooting Sports directly before planning a visit.

Seneca Lake Duck Hunters is a club-run archery range in Penn Yan, New York, in the Finger Lakes wine country region, and despite the waterfowl-focused name it maintains a field course for members. That points to a membership built around broader hunting and outdoor pursuits rather than archery alone, with the range likely serving as one piece of a larger sportsmen's operation. Field archery on rolling Finger Lakes terrain can be a solid way to build the judgment and shot-reading skills bowhunters need before deer or turkey season. Prospective members should contact the club directly to learn about dues, access policies, and whether the field course is open to guests.

Shady Oaks Gun Range in Cedar Park, just northwest of Austin, is primarily known by name as a firearms range but also maintains a field course for archery, giving Central Texas bowhunters a place to practice roving shots at varied distances rather than only flat-range target work. That kind of multi-discipline setup is common in Texas, where gun ranges often carve out archery space to serve hunters who use both a rifle and a bow depending on season. No pro shop or lesson program is confirmed here, so archers should plan to bring their own equipment. Call ahead to confirm the field course schedule and any range fees.

Mount Shasta, California sits in the shadow of one of the most striking peaks in the Cascade Range, and Shasta Mountain Archers is the volunteer-run archery club that gives local bowhunters and target archers a place to shoot in that dramatic Siskiyou County setting. As a volunteer club, it likely relies on member dues and work parties rather than paid staff to keep the range maintained, which is typical for rural Northern California archery groups. No specific programs, pro shop, or course features are documented for this listing. Anyone interested in shooting near Mount Shasta should contact the club directly to ask about membership and range access.

Colorado Springs has a strong outdoor and military-town culture, and Shatterproof Archery is one of the commercial archery ranges serving that Front Range population. The name suggests a focus on durable, high-performance gear or a no-nonsense approach to the sport, though no pro shop, lesson program, or course features are confirmed in this listing. That leaves it best understood as straightforward range access for archers who already have their own equipment and technique. Given how many archers pass through a city the size of Colorado Springs, a dedicated commercial range like this fills a real gap. Contact Shatterproof Archery directly for current hours and lane details.

Shelby County Archers in Sidney, Ohio runs a 3D course, giving local archers a chance to practice on foam animal targets at varying and unmarked distances rather than only flat paper targets. That kind of course is especially valuable heading into Ohio's deer season, since it trains the same instinctive range-judging skills bowhunters rely on in the field. As a club rather than a commercial operation, it likely operates on member support and volunteer upkeep. No pro shop or formal lesson program is listed, so newcomers should expect a bring-your-own-gear environment. Reach out directly to ask about membership, guest policies, and 3D shoot schedules.

Shelby Trails Archery Range is a volunteer-run, ASA-affiliated 3D archery club in Simpsonville, Kentucky, just east of Louisville. The Archery Shooters Association affiliation signals a course built and scored to a recognized competitive 3D standard, which matters for archers who want to test their skills against consistent, tournament-style target placements rather than a casual backyard setup. Being volunteer-run, the range likely depends on member involvement to maintain the course and run shoots throughout the season. No pro shop or lesson program is documented here. Kentucky bowhunters looking to sharpen distance judgment before whitetail season should contact the club directly about membership and shoot dates.

In Williston, Florida, in the heart of the state's horse country north of Ocala, Shell Pond Outdoors LLC operates as an ASA-affiliated 3D archery club despite its LLC name suggesting a more commercial structure. The ASA affiliation means the course follows Archery Shooters Association scoring conventions, appealing to bowhunters who want realistic distance and shot-angle practice on foam game targets. As a volunteer club, day-to-day operations likely lean on member participation rather than full-time staff. No pro shop or lessons are listed for this location. Florida archers curious about joining should reach out directly to confirm access, dues, and shoot-day schedules.

Strasburg sits in Virginia's Shenandoah Valley, and Shenandoah County Archers is the volunteer-run, ASA-affiliated 3D club that gives valley archers a place to shoot amid that landscape of farmland and ridgelines. The ASA affiliation points to a course designed around recognized 3D scoring standards rather than an informal layout, which is useful for archers preparing for regional shoots or simply wanting a more standardized challenge than a backyard range offers. No pro shop or lesson program is confirmed. Being volunteer-run, the club likely depends on its membership to maintain trails and targets. Contact Shenandoah County Archers directly to ask about membership and upcoming 3D shoot dates.

Sheridan, Wyoming sits at the base of the Bighorn Mountains, and Sheridan County Sportsmen is the club that gives local archers a place to shoot in that ranching and hunting-heavy part of the state. No pro shop, lesson program, 3D course, or field course is documented for this listing, so the range likely functions as core member-access shooting space rather than a full-service facility. That's a common model for sportsmen's clubs across rural Wyoming, where the emphasis is often on hunting, fishing, and shooting sports combined under one membership rather than archery alone. Contact the club directly to ask about membership requirements and range hours.

Sherwood Archers in Roanoke, Virginia runs both a 3D course and a field course, giving Blue Ridge-area archers two distinct disciplines at one volunteer-run club: foam-animal 3D targets for bowhunting practice and a field layout for the more technical, marked-and-unmarked-distance shooting that field archery demands. That dual setup is a step up from most single-course clubs in the region and suggests a membership invested in maintaining more than one style of range. No pro shop or lesson program is listed here. Roanoke-area archers interested in either discipline should contact the club directly to ask about membership, guest days, and course conditions.

Bedias is a small community in Grimes County, Texas, and Sherwood Archery is the commercial range serving that rural stretch between Houston and College Station. No pro shop, lessons, 3D course, or field course is confirmed for this listing, which suggests a simple range-access model rather than a full-service operation. For archers in this part of East Texas, having any dedicated commercial archery option nearby is notable given how spread out towns are in the area. Anyone planning to visit should call ahead, since small-town commercial ranges like this often keep limited or seasonal hours. Contact Sherwood Archery directly for current details.

A second Sherwood Archery, this one a volunteer-run club in Steubenville, Ohio along the West Virginia border, maintains a 3D course for members. The course gives Ohio Valley bowhunters a place to practice on foam animal targets at realistic, varied distances ahead of deer season, and as a volunteer operation it likely relies on member work days to keep the layout current. No pro shop or lesson program is documented. Steubenville's location along the Ohio River puts it within reach of archers from both Ohio and the West Virginia panhandle. Contact the club directly to confirm membership terms and 3D shoot schedules.

Sherwood Forest Bowmen, a fittingly named commercial archery operation in Sussex, Wisconsin just west of Milwaukee, runs a 3D course for archers who want foam-animal target practice rather than only flat paper targets. That kind of course is a strong fit for Wisconsin's deer-hunting culture, letting bowhunters rehearse distance estimation and shot placement before the season opens. No pro shop or lesson program is confirmed for this location, so equipment and instruction needs should be sorted elsewhere. Given the Robin Hood-inspired name, it's worth asking whether the club leans into any themed shoots. Contact Sherwood Forest Bowmen directly for course hours and access details.

Shoot Fire Shooters is a volunteer-run, ASA-affiliated 3D archery club in the small community of Muse, Oklahoma, in the state's southeastern corner near the Arkansas border. The Archery Shooters Association affiliation means the course is built to a recognized 3D scoring format, useful for archers preparing for regional competitions or just wanting standardized foam-target practice. As with most volunteer clubs, expect the range to be maintained by member effort rather than paid staff, and hours or shoot dates to follow a club calendar rather than fixed business hours. No pro shop or lesson program is listed. Contact the club directly for membership and shoot-day information.

Shooting Star Archery Academy Inc in Pipersville, Pennsylvania, in the Bucks County countryside northwest of Philadelphia, is a USA Archery affiliated club built around a Junior Olympic Archery Development program. JOAD gives young archers a structured, age-appropriate path from first-timer basics up toward competitive Olympic-style recurve shooting, backed by USA Archery's coaching and safety framework rather than an informal setup. For Bucks County families looking for a serious youth archery pathway rather than a one-off lesson, that JOAD structure is the key differentiator here. No pro shop or general lesson program beyond JOAD is documented. Contact the academy directly to ask about age groups and enrollment.

Shooting Zone in Hackensack, New Jersey, just across the Hudson from Manhattan, is a USA Archery affiliated club running both a Junior Olympic Archery Development program and an Adult Archery Program, with lessons available for those getting started. That combination means the club serves families end to end, from kids working through JOAD's structured skill levels to parents picking up the sport alongside them, all under USA Archery's coaching framework. For a densely populated part of North Jersey, having a club that covers both age groups in one place is a real convenience. Contact Shooting Zone directly for class schedules and enrollment details.

Show Me Shooting Sports in Independence, Missouri, part of the Kansas City metro, is a USA Archery affiliated hybrid club that runs three distinct programs: Junior Olympic Archery Development, an Adult Archery Program, and 3D Archery. That range of offerings covers Olympic-style recurve development for kids, structured entry for adult beginners, and foam-target 3D practice for hunters, making it one of the more full-featured clubs in the area rather than a single-discipline operation. No pro shop or standalone lesson listing is confirmed beyond those named programs. Kansas City-area archers of any age or interest should contact Show Me Shooting Sports directly to find the right program.

Shrewd Outdoors in Salem, Virginia, in the Roanoke Valley, is a USA Archery affiliated club that pairs a genuinely broad program lineup, Junior Olympic Archery Development, an Adult Archery Program, and 3D Archery, with an on-site pro shop and lessons. That combination of youth development, adult entry, hunting-style 3D practice, retail support, and instruction under one roof makes it one of the more complete archery operations in southwest Virginia rather than a single-purpose range. Families and adult beginners alike can get outfitted and coached without needing a separate stop. Contact Shrewd Outdoors directly to ask about class schedules, pro shop inventory, and JOAD enrollment.

Silicon Valley Archery Development is a volunteer-run archery club in Palo Alto, California, giving Bay Area archers a foothold in a region far better known for tech campuses than open range space. No pro shop, lesson program, or course features are documented for this listing, so it likely functions as member-access shooting space maintained through volunteer effort rather than a full-service operation. Finding any dedicated archery club in the dense, expensive Peninsula real estate market is itself notable, since land for a range is hard to come by there. Anyone interested in the South Bay archery scene should contact the club directly about membership and access.

Silver Arrow Bowmen in Mount Vernon, Washington, in the Skagit Valley north of Seattle, runs a field course and maintains 14 lanes, giving local archers a genuinely sized layout for both flat-range and field-style shooting. Fourteen lanes is enough to accommodate group shoots or club tournaments without long waits, and the field course adds the marked and unmarked distance variety that keeps field archery distinct from simple target shooting. No pro shop or lesson program is listed for this club-run range. Skagit Valley archers looking for a well-equipped local option should contact Silver Arrow Bowmen directly about membership and course access.

Silver Bow Archers takes its name from Butte, Montana's home county, Silver Bow, and gives local archers a club-run place to shoot in a city with deep mining and outdoor heritage. No pro shop, lessons, 3D course, or field course is documented here, suggesting straightforward member-access range space rather than a full-service facility. Montana's hunting culture makes any dedicated archery club a useful resource, even a modest one, for bowhunters tuning up before elk or deer season in the surrounding mountains. Contact Silver Bow Archers directly to ask about membership, range hours, and whether guest shooting is available.

Silver City Archery Co is a volunteer-run, ASA-affiliated 3D club in Silver City, New Mexico, tucked in the Gila National Forest region of the state's southwest corner. The Archery Shooters Association affiliation points to a course built around recognized 3D scoring, which matters to archers wanting realistic foam-target practice ahead of hunting season in the surrounding high-desert and forest terrain. Being volunteer-run, the club likely depends on member turnout to keep courses maintained and shoots scheduled rather than operating on fixed commercial hours. No pro shop or lesson program is listed. Contact the club directly for membership details and 3D shoot dates.

Silver Creek Metro Park Archery Range is a public archery range inside the Silver Creek Metro Park system in Doylestown, Ohio, giving Summit County residents free or low-cost access to a dedicated shooting area within a larger park setting rather than a private club or commercial operation. No pro shop, lessons, or course features are confirmed for this listing, which fits the typical model for a metro park range: open access during park hours rather than programming or retail. That makes it a solid low-barrier entry point for anyone in the Akron area who wants to try archery without a membership. Contact the metro park system directly for current hours and rules.

Silver Eagles Archery is a volunteer-run, ASA-affiliated 3D club in Wheelersburg, Ohio, along the Ohio River in the southern part of the state. Its Archery Shooters Association affiliation means the course follows recognized 3D competition standards, appealing to archers who want their foam-target practice to translate directly to regional ASA shoots rather than just casual backyard scoring. As a volunteer operation, upkeep of the course and scheduling of shoots likely runs on member participation rather than paid staff. No pro shop or lesson program is documented. Southern Ohio archers interested in joining should contact the club directly for dues and shoot-day schedules.

Silver Springs Archers Inc. is an ASA-affiliated archery club in Ocala, Florida, near the natural springs the city is named for, though the affiliation record on file shows a status of expired as of 2025. That doesn't necessarily mean the club has closed, affiliation lapses can happen for administrative reasons, but it's worth confirming current status before assuming active ASA-sanctioned shoots are still running there. No pro shop or lesson program is listed for this location. Central Florida archers interested in Silver Springs Archers should contact the club directly to verify whether membership, meetings, and range access are still active.

Silverado Archery Club sits in Napa, California, better known worldwide for wine country than for archery, giving local residents a volunteer-run place to shoot amid that agricultural landscape. No pro shop, lesson program, or course features are documented for this listing, so it most likely offers straightforward member-access range space maintained by the club rather than a full commercial operation. For Napa Valley locals, having any dedicated archery club nearby is a niche but real amenity in a region built around vineyards rather than shooting sports. Contact Silverado Archery Club directly to ask about membership and range availability.

Singers Glen Bowbenders Club, in the small Shenandoah Valley community of Singers Glen, Virginia, runs both a 3D course and a field course and is listed in the International Bowhunting Organization's pro shop directory. That dual-course setup gives valley archers both the foam-animal realism of 3D shooting and the marked and unmarked distance discipline of field archery in one place, while the IBO directory listing points to a hunting-oriented, competition-aware operation rather than a purely casual range. For bowhunters in the Shenandoah Valley wanting to sharpen both skill sets before deer season, this is a notably well-rounded option. Contact the club directly for course access and hours.

Singletary Rod & Gun Club in Oxford, Massachusetts is listed in the International Bowhunting Organization's pro shop directory, signaling a hunting-focused archery presence within what its name suggests is a broader multi-discipline sportsmen's club covering both firearms and archery. No 3D course, field course, or lesson program is separately confirmed for the archery side of the operation. Central Massachusetts archers and bowhunters looking for a club with hunting-community ties, rather than a purely recreational target range, may find this a good fit. Contact Singletary Rod & Gun Club directly to ask about archery-specific access, membership requirements, and range availability.

SiWen Archery in Laingsburg, Michigan, north of Lansing, is a USA Archery affiliated club running an unusually complete lineup: Junior Olympic Archery Development, an Adult Archery Program, Olympic Archery in the Schools, and lessons. That combination reaches archers at nearly every entry point, from school-age kids introduced through classroom partnerships to dedicated JOAD athletes to adult beginners taking private or group lessons. Few clubs in mid-Michigan cover that full a spread of programming under USA Archery's coaching and safety standards. No pro shop is listed for this location. Contact SiWen Archery directly for program schedules and enrollment information.

Skookum Archers Club & Range in Puyallup, Washington, in the Puget Sound lowlands south of Tacoma, combines a field course with lessons, giving both experienced archers and newcomers a reason to visit. The field course offers the marked and unmarked distance variety that separates field archery from flat target shooting, while the lesson program means beginners aren't left to figure out form and safety on their own. No pro shop is confirmed for this club-run range. For South Sound archers wanting both instruction and a proper field layout in one place, Skookum stands out. Contact the club directly for lesson scheduling and membership details.

Slingin' Arrows is a commercial archery range in El Dorado, Arkansas, in the oil-and-timber country of the state's south, giving local archers a dedicated place to shoot outside of backyard setups. No pro shop, lesson program, 3D course, or field course is documented for this listing, so it likely operates as a simple pay-to-shoot range rather than a full-service center. In a smaller South Arkansas city, having any commercial archery option at all fills a real need for archers without their own land to shoot on. Contact Slingin' Arrows directly for current hours and lane pricing before visiting.

Smith Point Archery Lanes in Patchogue, New York, on Long Island's South Shore, is a commercial range that pairs indoor lanes with both a pro shop and lessons, making it a full-service stop for archers who want to shoot, get outfitted, and get coached without visiting three different businesses. That's a meaningful convenience on Long Island, where dedicated archery space is limited and often shared with other sports facilities. Beginners can pick up gear and book a lesson in the same visit, while more experienced shooters can just come in and use the lanes. Contact Smith Point Archery Lanes directly for lesson availability and lane hours.

Smith Point JOAD, also based in Patchogue, New York, is a USA Archery affiliated club running a Junior Olympic Archery Development program alongside an Adult Archery Program and lessons. The JOAD structure gives young Long Island archers a defined, skill-level-based path toward Olympic-style recurve competition, backed by USA Archery's coaching standards, while the adult program and lessons extend that same structured approach to grown-up beginners. Between JOAD athletes and adults just starting out, the club covers a wide age range under one roof. No pro shop is listed for this club. Contact Smith Point JOAD directly for enrollment and class schedule information.

Smoky Mountain Archers is a volunteer-run archery club in Knoxville, Tennessee, putting East Tennessee archers within easy reach of the Great Smoky Mountains for both practice and eventual bowhunting trips into that terrain. No pro shop, lesson program, 3D course, or field course is documented for this listing, so expect member-access range space maintained through volunteer effort rather than a commercial facility. For a metro area the size of Knoxville, a club like this gives archers without private land a reliable local option. Contact Smoky Mountain Archers directly to ask about membership and range access policies.

Smythe County Archery Club in Marion, Virginia, in the mountains of the state's southwest corner, is listed in the International Bowhunting Organization's pro shop directory, pointing to a hunting-oriented archery presence in this Smyth County community. No 3D course, field course, or lesson program is separately confirmed for this listing. Southwest Virginia's rugged terrain makes it strong bowhunting country, and a club with IBO ties suggests a customer base geared toward that pursuit rather than purely Olympic-style target shooting. Local archers and hunters should contact Smythe County Archery Club directly to confirm range access, hours, and whether retail support is available on site.

Sod Archery Club takes its name from the tiny community of Sod, West Virginia, deep in the state's rural interior, and operates as a volunteer-run, ASA-affiliated 3D club there. The Archery Shooters Association affiliation means the course is built to recognized 3D scoring standards, giving West Virginia bowhunters realistic foam-target practice ahead of the state's deer and bear seasons in that mountainous terrain. As with most volunteer clubs, expect shoot schedules and course upkeep to run on member involvement rather than fixed commercial hours. No pro shop or lesson program is listed. Contact the club directly for membership information and 3D shoot dates.
